newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore govt to monitor Caltex 100-octane petrol.
newsitem.headline: Singapore govt to monitor Caltex 100-octane petrol.

text.p: Singapore's Environment Ministry said on Tuesday it will closely monitor the benzene content of the 100-octane unleaded petrol introduced by Caltex last week to ensure that it does not exceed the five-percent limit.
U.S. major Caltex was the first oil company to launch the 100-octane unleaded grade petrol in Singapore on July 17.
Caltex officials held a meeting with officials from the ministry after the launch, company and ministry sources said.

Caltex, a joint-venture between U.S. majors Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc, said the higher octane number and the company's special additive Techron would boost engine performance, enhance fuel economy and reduce emissions.
Caltex's move immediately drew flak from its rivals who said they saw no benefit in terms of improving performance of Japanese cars, but could worsen air pollution.
The majority of cars on Singapore roads are Japanese models.
Caltex said that the benzene content was between four and five percent, a level deemed safe by the industry.
The ministry said in response to a Reuters query that the benzene content in any petrol sold in Singapore should not exceed five percent.
"This five-percent limit is the same as that adopted in the EU," the statement said, referring to the European Union.

"Caltex has confirmed that methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) was used to produce 100-octane rating and that there is no difference in the benzene content between the new 100-octane petrol and the 98-octane petrol previously sold by Caltex."
The ministry also said Singapore has not set a standard for aromatics and olefin content in petrol.
